title: Emulated: The Data for Fully Autonomous Software Engineers and Companies — Joseph Wang
talk_summary: Joseph Wang and Sid of Emulated argue that agent capability gaps are data gaps: frontier benchmarks only exercise in-repo code diffs, not the surrounding organizational and infrastructure context (tickets, postmortems, deployments, live traffic, blast radius). They describe containerized 'company' environments and, beyond single-node sandboxes, multi-node sandboxes with real cloud resources to train/evaluate agents on long-horizon infra work.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build task environments that include the organizational context around the code (tickets, projects, incidents, customer conversations, postmortems) plus operational constraints, so agents are evaluated on end-to-end work rather than a single PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tasks only operate within the code base ... it doesn't do all of the work that a human does

takeaways.technique: Multi-node sandbox with real infra for heavy/long-horizon runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue single-container sandboxes break down once a task needs provisioning, deployment, rolling updates, or failure injection, and move to multi-node sandboxes with access to real cloud resources ('put a cloud in a box').
takeaways.evidence_quote: Beyond beyond a certain threshold, there is a critical mass at which sandboxing on a single node uh can only get you so far.

takeaways.technique: Simulate the whole company, not just the engineer
takeaways.what_they_do: They containerize an entire software company including PM/customer-facing roles and incidents, so agents must reason across roles and handoffs rather than only writing code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We've taken software engineering companies and we've put them into containerized environments.

takeaways.technique: Inject operational failures into the task, not just unit tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Environments include flapping nodes, lagging learners, stale/deprecated nodes, and rolling deployments that conflict, forcing the agent to reason about failures in real time under live traffic.
